chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

"When a man accuses his wife [of adultery] and then contradicts himself [by retracting or being proven wrong], he is flogged with the fixed penalty and she remains his wife; and if he does not contradict himself [his accusation stands], they undergo li'an (mutual imprecation) and are separated from each other."

key_terms.جُلِدَ الْحَدَّ: He was flogged with the fixed penalty
key_terms.قَذَفَ: To accuse (specifically of adultery without witnesses)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between qadhf and li'an in Shia jurisprudence regarding marital accusations?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the procedural distinction in Shia jurisprudence between a simple false accusation (qadhf) and the specific ritual of mutual imprecation (li'an). It establishes that if the husband contradicts his claim, he is merely flogged and the marriage persists, whereas a standing accusation triggers li'an, resulting in permanent separation. This ruling underscores the gravity of li'an as a mechanism for resolving uncertainty in paternity and marital fidelity within the family structure.
